Meaning: The maker declares a metal or mineral powder load (copper, bronze, brass, steel, iron, tungsten, magnetite) that makes the filament far denser than its base polymer. It is a grade of the polymer's material with the load quoted in Composition / filler (R095); the physics windows judge it as a dense-filled grade (D80), and the estimate model keeps its values from pulling the family.
A declared additive (hollow microspheres, a foaming agent) lowers the density well below the base polymer's; stiffness and strength may move with it.

A declared plasticiser lowers the density, the modulus and the softening point well below the neat polymer's; a plasticised PVC is a different material from the rigid one and its published values are its own.
The published density or stiffness is beyond what the unfilled base polymer can reach, so the product contains a filler its maker does not name.

The maker declares a flame-retardant ceramic load in the named polymer but publishes no loading fraction. The product's values remain its own; the estimate model treats it as a declared grade variant without inferring density or qualification.

The maker declares a flexible or elastomeric grade of the named polymer (an elastomer-modified or low-comonomer grade, R098). Its density, modulus and softening point sit below the rigid polymer’s, it foams nothing, and the estimate model keeps its values from pulling the family.

A glow-in-the-dark pigment (strontium aluminate) the maker names in the product. Makers of glow filaments say it wears brass nozzles, so the product is not its polymer's printer-guide type and reads no guide row (D129); its values stay its own, and the estimate model keeps them from pulling the family (D131).

A PLA grade its maker formulates to crystallise in the print, where plain PLA stays glassy: its sheet shows it without annealing (a Vicat or heat deflection far above the glass transition as printed, a crystallisation peak, or heat resistance stated "without annealing"). It prints as its type, so it reads its printer maker's guide row and its kind of plastic's chamber need (TRUE beside); its values stay its own, apart from the material's spread, and the estimate model keeps them from pulling the family (D154).

A filler, named or not, that the product's documents sell for its look, a matte finish or a glitter, and for no function. Its density sits above the neat polymer's, as a dense filler's does, but nothing on the product's documents says the filler changes how it prints. It prints as its type, so it reads its printer maker's guide row in full (nozzle, bed, chamber, enclosure, the hardened-nozzle answer and drying) and its kind of plastic's chamber need (TRUE beside); the product's own statements still come first (D175). Not a metal powder, which its makers say wears a brass nozzle (colorFabb of its steelFill, Protopasta of its stainless steel and iron fills; D129), nor a glow pigment, nor a load sold for a function (flame retardance, X-ray shielding, zero warp). Its values stay its own, apart from the material's spread, and the estimate model keeps them from pulling the family.
